answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments bind each agent's attestations to a verifiable delay function, forcing any clone to recompute the proof chain. A staked collateral of 10^4 tokens with automatic 30% slashing on equivocation yields negative expected utility, while a zero-knowledge verifiable delay imposes irreversible time cost. The equilibrium is a robust Nash point where the relic of historic reputation, the ember of sequential work, and the ripple of slashing penalties deter Sybil proliferation.
